Review: BBT203/BBT230 by (OAH)
Classroom Environment:
Sir has an unparalleled ability to connect with his students. His style is unique and refreshing. He feels less like a formal lecturer and more like an experienced older brother "মাঠে আড্ডা দেয়ার বড় ভাই" who is sharing his knowledge. Personally, it felt really easy to engage with him in and out of the class. His classes are full of jokes, he has a funny sass and light-hearted roasting(the one getting roasted may not like it depends if they lack a thick skin). This is his signature style. It's sarcastic, has an underlying roasting feels but not insulting if you shrug it off/give a counter/hahahaha move on... or you can stay completely quiet and mind your own business, you'll be safe. In our section, I was his go to student to bicker with প্রতিবেশী ভাবীদের মতো ঝগড়া করতাম(with no disrespect in mind; all fun) He covers the planned topics for the day and then ends the class, regardless of how much time is left. There's no dragging it out. Several times, he finished a complete and clear lecture in less than an hour and dismissed the class because everyone understood the material (this was before the back to back class cancellings, so he was chill about it). He has this craving to run to his office and relax there, you can sense it right after the lecture is over lol. The moment he gets out of his class, visit him in the office, he won't stand around.
Teaching Style:
He primarily teaches verbally and writes precise notes and flowcharts on the board. He breaks down methods into clear, logical steps (example: Method 1, Method 2, If Type A then do this, if type B then do that etc.). He avoids unnecessary jargon and gets straight to the point. He focuses only on the topics you will actually need and apply in the future. He doesn't follow specific lecture slides or a textbook. His lectures are self contained and all you need. Yet he will upload like 4 books on Canvas and throughout the semester some necessary online softwares, his own calendar for the semester, tables and lecture notes if he thinks it's necessary(we needed them). He says like "The topics are going to stay the same no matter which book you follow, google to practice, ask ChatGPT... don't ask me from where to practice, use your common sense!" He is all about learning the core concepts. That's why his class notes are more than enough to master the topics, if you don't study anything else but the notes, you'll still be able to answer.
Grading & Assessments:
Class Tests (20+25 marks): There were two class tests, originally worth 20 marks each. The tests typically had two main questions where you had to understand a scenario and apply the correct formulas to solve them. The second CT was converted to 25 marks. He gave 5 extra marks on top of what you got from the test to adjust the midterm weightage due to missed classes.
Final Exam (30 marks):
20 marks: A practical question where you had to box only the final answers, with no need to show the process. But you need to be good on calculator.
10 marks: Conceptual MCQs covering the entire course. These were easy for anyone who attended class regularly, as they tested your understanding of the concepts, not math.
Partial Credit: You won't get a flat zero for a math error. He gives "খয়রাতি" charity marks based on your approach, understanding and how correctly you proceeded.
TLDR:
For 252 session, he was an exceptional professor who made complex topics engaging and straightforward. His questions were very standard—>easy and he didn't need to "curve" because of his charity markings on the CTs(20+25), MT(25) and Final(30). Yes, for an ideal semester he has no attendance+class participation marks, no assignments in his outline. Personally I would say, he is great for both learning and getting a good grade for a proper student who actually paid attention or utilized his office hours. More importantly, he made math fun! Before doing this course I saw so many mixed comments about him that even I got confused and was hesitant at first but now I wish I had him for BUS172(prerequisite to this course) haha!
